# Halo

Halo is an iPhone app for logging migraine attacks and, over time, everything that might trigger them. A Go backend on
my home computer stores all data, transcribes spoken summaries with Whisper, extracts attack details with a model, and
records the weather around every attack.

This is a proof of concept for personal use. Health data never lives on the phone.

## Layout

- `app/`: Expo app (React Native, TypeScript), run in Expo Go
- `backend/`: Go service that owns the database, recordings, and weather
- `deploy/`: systemd units and backup scripts

## Prerequisites

- Go 1.27.1 or newer (`go version` must print `go1.27.1` or later)
- Node 24 LTS (`app/.nvmrc` pins it; run `nvm use` in `app/`)
- Expo Go on your iPhone, signed in to your Expo account. Also run `npx expo login` on the computer.

## Running the app

Scan the QR code with the iPhone camera to open the app in Expo Go. The App Store version of Expo Go only supports the
latest SDK, so after a new SDK release run `npx expo install expo@latest && npx expo install --fix`.

CI does not check Expo package versions because new Expo patch releases would fail it at random. After upgrading
Expo or adding a package, run `npm run deps:check` in `app` and fix any mismatches with `npx expo install --fix`.

## End-to-end tests

See `app/e2e/README.md` for how to run the Maestro flows on the iOS Simulator.

A Go package turns a voice-summary transcript into a validated

: it builds the prompt (transcript, attack, medicine list, timezone, recording time), asks the model for structured output, and drops or repairs anything invalid with a warning. It never guesses a medicine.

package extract

const PromptVersion = "1"

type Input struct {
	Transcript  string
	Attack      model.Attack
	Medications []model.Medication
	RecordedAt  time.Time
}

type RawDose struct {
	Medication string   `json:"medication"`
	Amount     *float64 `json:"amount"`
	TakenAt    *string  `json:"taken_at"`
}

type Raw struct {
	StartedAt    *string   `json:"started_at"`
	EndedAt      *string   `json:"ended_at"`
	PeakSeverity *int      `json:"peak_severity"`
	Symptoms     []string  `json:"symptoms"`
	Doses        []RawDose `json:"doses"`
	Notes        *string   `json:"notes"`
}

func Validate(raw Raw, attack model.Attack, meds []model.Medication, recordedAt time.Time) model.Proposal

func New(client llm.Client) *Extractor
func (e *Extractor) Extract(ctx context.Context, in Input) (model.Proposal, error)
func (e *Extractor) ModelName() string
Validation rules (all produce a warning string in

| Input | Result |
|---|---|
| `started_at` / `ended_at` / dose `taken_at` not RFC 3339 | dropped: `dropped <field>: not a valid time` |
| a time after `recordedAt` | dropped: `dropped <field>: after the recording time` |
| a time more than 7 days before `recordedAt` | dropped: `dropped <field>: more than 7 days before the recording` |
| `ended_at` before the effective start (proposed `started_at`, else `attack.StartedAt`) | dropped: `dropped ended_at: before the start` |
| `peak_severity` outside 0 to 10 | dropped: `dropped peak_severity: <n> is outside 0 to 10` |
| symptom not in `model.Symptoms` (after trim and lower-case) | dropped: `dropped unknown symptom "<s>"` |
| duplicate symptom | kept once, no warning |
| dose medicine name equal (case-insensitive, trimmed) to a non-archived medicine | `ProposedDose` with that medicine's id |
| dose medicine name with no exact match (including nicknames like "riza") | `UnknownMedication{Name, Amount, TakenAt}`, no warning; never fuzzy-matched |
| matched dose with `amount` null | usual amount, no warning |
| matched dose with `amount` <= 0 | usual amount: `used usual amount for <name>: <n> is not a positive amount` |
| matched dose with `taken_at` null or dropped | effective start: `used attack start as the time for <name>` |
| `notes` empty after trim | null, no warning |
All times in the result are converted to UTC. All slices in the result are non-nil.
